A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NetDiff for directional ad hoc network topology and parity generation. Their text, equations, figures, and tables are readable, including v2's appendices in Sections 7–10. v1 has no appendix. Changed experimental settings limit direct performance comparisons but do not prevent a reliable document comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original topology-generation experiments, simulated throughput, architectural and loss ablations in Tables 1–3, and execution timings.

after.justification: v2 reports original baseline comparisons, component ablations, mobility-reconfiguration experiments, and quantitative 32-node results, including Appendix 9.

M1.justification: v2 introduces ACAM with unnormalized cosine-similarity aggregation and pooled global FiLM modulation, extending v1's CAM mechanism with node-dependent modulation. The cosine loss gains predicted-edge weighting. Algorithm 2 also changes substantially: parity/interference filtering, throughput-based connectivity repair, and connectivity-preserving pruning replace the simpler sector pruning and distance-based reconnection.

E1.justification: v2 extends actual evaluation from topology generation to updates under node movement, testing standard and minor reconfigurations in Section 5.2 and Tables 5–6. v1 proposed these procedures without reporting corresponding experiments. Quantitative 32-node tables expand evidence for a network size already mentioned as tested in v1.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's graph-transformer and component comparisons, v2 evaluates GraphVAE and GT-VAE in Table 1, and omnidirectional, Huang et al., and MST+greedy comparators in Table 2. It also separately compares CAM and ACAM variants. These are evaluated additions, rather than citation changes or simple baseline renaming.

E3.justification: Reported settings change from 10 to 5 transformer blocks and from learning rates of 10^-4–10^-7 to a linear 10^-3–10^-6 schedule. Supervision changes from greedy construction to quasi-exhaustive search with a greedy fallback. v2 replaces per-user throughput reporting with link and sum-rate measures, introduces mobility-testing protocols, and specifies mixed 16/32-node retraining in Appendix 9.

E4.justification: v1 already contains architectural-feature and loss ablations. v2 extends these with explicit CAM-versus-ACAM comparisons, token-count sensitivity reporting approximately 0.8% lower saturation with 16 versus 1 tokens, and capacity-related observations. Section 5.2 and Figures 3–4 add continuity/speed analyses and examples of topology reconfiguration under movement.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates only. v2 adds ± values to selected saturation and constraint results in Tables 1 and 3–5 and discloses random seed 123. It does not define those uncertainty quantities or report a repeat count, so the additions do not establish repeated-seed experiments or a specified statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Core results are revised under changed settings: v1 reports 99.13% NetDiff connectivity, whereas v2 reports 98.68% for both CAM and ACAM. New results include NetDiff throughput upper bounds of 78.92 and 322.40 Mbps for 16 and 32 nodes, mobility continuity/speed measurements, and Appendix 9's size results. Isolated-node and range-compliance entries disappear. These changes do not establish controlled cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 revises the attention and cosine-loss definitions, introduces explicit layout-distribution and perturbation assumptions in Section 2.3, and defines a parity-gated sum-rate/interference model in Appendix 8. These are limited formal-model extensions; neither version supplies theorems or proofs. Fuller joint edge/parity notation elaborates a capability already described in v1.

C1.justification: v2 redefines the token contribution around absolute, count-sensitive global control and adds abstract claims of exceeding 95% of target performance, constant inference time, and superiority to heuristic and omnidirectional baselines. v1 emphasized realistic topologies and CAM-based global coherence without these quantified comparative claims. Partial diffusion remains an existing contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a counting/density explanation for ACAM and materially qualifies applicability: comparable 32-node performance requires training exposure, networks above 40 nodes are excluded, and throughput is an upper bound excluding routing and multichannel scheduling. Algorithm 2 also acknowledges possible residual disconnection, whereas v1 described correction as ensuring connectivity.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information with feature width, batch size, epoch limit, weight-decay scheduling, early stopping, coordinate normalization, and the 15,000-sample mixed-size retraining procedure. Appendices add detailed generation/correction pseudocode and the physical performance model. Exact simulation parameters remain unavailable and are explicitly identified as proprietary.

R1.justification: Related work expands from a largely descriptive overview to detailed positioning around node conditioning, permutation invariance, and limitations of autoregressive, spectral, flow, and reinforcement-learning approaches. New discussions include GraphRNN, SPECTRE, DIFUSCO, virtual nodes, and directional-network methods. v2 also distinguishes TopoFormer by its lack of joint topology-parity prediction.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, architecture explanation, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work becomes an introduction subsection, network evolution moves before the architecture, and features/losses become a separate section. Generation and correction algorithms move into new appendices. The title, author list, and publication header also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, adds a network illustration and two reconfiguration figures, and redraws the CAM architecture as ACAM. The diffusion illustration is retained with a revised caption. Existing benchmark tables are restructured, additional baseline/mobility/size tables appear, and expanded algorithms are relocated to the appendices.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for central claims: v1's mobility proposal gains quantitative continuity and speed evaluation, while broader generative and networking baselines and CAM/ACAM comparisons better test the proposed architecture. Expanded implementation details and explicit size-generalization limits improve assessability. These gains address important validation gaps, despite undefined uncertainty values and proprietary simulation parameters that still limit reproducibility. Changed settings prevent interpreting the revision as a controlled performance improvement.
